log_file.description: The main log file where service and host events are logged.

nagios_generated_cfg.description: The path to the sitesummary generated Nagios configuration file.

object_cache_file.description: The file where object definitions are cached when Nagios starts/restarts.

precached_object_file.description: The location of the precached object file.

resource_file.description: An optional resource file that contains $USERx$ macro definitions.

status_file.description: The file where the current status of all monitored services and hosts is stored.

status_update_interval.description: The frequency (in seconds) that Nagios will periodically dump program, host, and service status data.

nagios_user.description: The effective user that Nagios should run as.

nagios_group.description: The effective group that Nagios should run as.

check_external_commands.description: Whether or not Nagios should check for external commands (0 = disable, 1 = enable).

command_check_interval.description: The interval at which Nagios should check for external commands.

command_file.description: The file that Nagios checks for external command requests.

external_command_buffer_slots.description: The number of items or 'slots' that the Nagios daemon should allocate to the buffer for external commands.

lock_file.description: The lockfile that Nagios will use to store its PID number.

temp_file.description: A temporary file that is used as scratch space when Nagios updates the status log, etc.

temp_path.description: Path where Nagios can create temp files for service and host check results.

event_broker_options.description: Controls what (if any) data gets sent to the event broker (-1 = Broker everything).

log_rotation_method.description: The log rotation method (n=none, h=hourly, d=daily, w=weekly, m=monthly).

log_archive_path.description: The directory where archived (rotated) log files should be placed.

use_syslog.description: Whether messages should be logged to the syslog facility (1 = yes, 0 = no).

log_notifications.description: Whether notifications should be logged (1 = yes, 0 = no).

log_service_retries.description: Whether service check retries should be logged (1 = yes, 0 = no).

log_host_retries.description: Whether host check retries should be logged (1 = yes, 0 = no).

log_event_handlers.description: Whether host and service event handlers should be logged (1 = yes, 0 = no).

log_initial_states.description: Whether Nagios should log all initial host and service states (1 = yes, 0 = no).

log_external_commands.description: Whether Nagios should log external commands (1 = yes, 0 = no).

log_passive_checks.description: Whether Nagios should log passive host and service checks (1 = yes, 0 = no).

service_inter_check_delay_method.description: The method for initially spreading out service checks (n=none, d=dumb, s=smart).

max_service_check_spread.description: The timeframe (in minutes) from program start that an initial check of all services should be completed.

service_interleave_factor.description: How service checks are interleaved (s=smart, x=interleave factor).

host_inter_check_delay_method.description: The method for initially spreading out host checks (n=none, d=dumb, s=smart).

max_host_check_spread.description: The timeframe (in minutes) from program start that an initial check of all hosts should be completed.

max_concurrent_checks.description: The maximum number of service checks that can be run in parallel (0 = no restriction).

check_result_reaper_frequency.description: The frequency (in seconds) that Nagios will process the results of host and service checks.

max_check_result_reaper_time.description: The max amount of time (in seconds) that a single check result reaper event will be allowed to run.

check_result_path.description: Directory where Nagios stores the results of host and service checks that have not yet been processed.

max_check_result_file_age.description: The maximum age (in seconds) which check result files are considered to be valid.

cached_host_check_horizon.description: The maximum amount of time (in seconds) that the state of a previous host check is considered current.

cached_service_check_horizon.description: The maximum amount of time (in seconds) that the state of a previous service check is considered current.

enable_predictive_host_dependency_checks.description: Whether Nagios will attempt to execute checks of hosts for predictive dependency logic (0 = disable, 1 = enable).

enable_predictive_service_dependency_che.description: Whether Nagios will attempt to execute checks of service for predictive dependency logic (0 = disable, 1 = enable).

soft_state_dependencies.description: Whether Nagios will use soft state information when checking dependencies (0 = no, 1 = yes).

auto_reschedule_checks.description: Whether Nagios will attempt to automatically reschedule active checks (0 = no, 1 = yes).

auto_rescheduling_interval.description: How often (in seconds) Nagios will attempt to automatically reschedule checks.

auto_rescheduling_window.description: The 'window' of time (in seconds) that Nagios will look at when automatically rescheduling checks.

sleep_time.description: The number of seconds to sleep between checking for system events and service checks.

service_check_timeout.description: Maximum time allotted for service checks (in seconds).

host_check_timeout.description: Maximum time allotted for host checks (in seconds).

event_handler_timeout.description: Maximum time allotted for event handlers (in seconds).

notification_timeout.description: Maximum time allotted for notifications (in seconds).

ocsp_timeout.description: Maximum time allotted for ocsp command (in seconds).

perfdata_timeout.description: Maximum time allotted for performance data commands (in seconds).

retain_state_information.description: Whether Nagios will save state information for services and hosts before shutting down (0 = no, 1 = yes).

state_retention_file.description: The file that Nagios should use to store host and service state information before it shuts down.

retention_update_interval.description: How often (in minutes) that Nagios will automatically save retention data during normal operation.

use_retained_program_state.description: Whether Nagios will set program status variables based on values saved in the retention file (0 = no, 1 = yes).

use_retained_scheduling_info.description: Whether Nagios will retain scheduling info based on values saved in the retention file (0 = no, 1 = yes).

retained_host_attribute_mask.description: Bitmask of host attributes that are not retained by Nagios during program restarts.

retained_service_attribute_mask.description: Bitmask of service attributes that are not retained by Nagios during program restarts.

retained_process_host_attribute_mask.description: Bitmask of process attributes (host options) that are not retained.

retained_process_service_attribute_mask.description: Bitmask of process attributes (service options) that are not retained.

retained_contact_host_attribute_mask.description: Bitmask of contact attributes (host options) that are not retained.

retained_contact_service_attribute_mask.description: Bitmask of contact attributes (service options) that are not retained.

interval_length.description: The seconds per unit interval as used in the host/contact/service configuration files.

use_aggressive_host_checking.description: Whether to enable aggressive host checking features (0 = no, 1 = yes).

execute_service_checks.description: Whether Nagios will actively execute service checks when it initially starts (0 = no, 1 = yes).

accept_passive_service_checks.description: Whether Nagios will accept passive service checks results when it initially (re)starts (0 = no, 1 = yes).

execute_host_checks.description: Whether Nagios will actively execute host checks when it initially starts (0 = no, 1 = yes).

accept_passive_host_checks.description: Whether Nagios will accept passive host checks results when it initially (re)starts (0 = no, 1 = yes).

enable_notifications.description: Whether Nagios will send out any host or service notifications when it is initially (re)started (0 = no, 1 = yes).

enable_event_handlers.description: Whether Nagios will run any host or service event handlers when it is initially (re)started (0 = no, 1 = yes).

process_performance_data.description: Whether Nagios will process performance data returned from service and host checks (0 = no, 1 = yes).

obsess_over_services.description: Whether Nagios will obsess over service checks and run the ocsp_command (0 = no, 1 = yes).

obsess_over_hosts.description: Whether Nagios will obsess over host checks and run the ochp_command (0 = no, 1 = yes).

translate_passive_host_checks.description: Whether Nagios will translate DOWN/UNREACHABLE passive host check results into their proper state (0 = no, 1 = yes).

passive_host_checks_are_soft.description: Whether Nagios will treat passive host checks as being HARD or SOFT (0 = HARD, 1 = SOFT).

check_for_orphaned_services.description: Whether Nagios will periodically check for orphaned service checks (0 = no, 1 = yes).

check_for_orphaned_hosts.description: Whether Nagios will periodically check for orphaned host checks (0 = no, 1 = yes).

check_service_freshness.description: Whether Nagios will periodically check the 'freshness' of service results (0 = no, 1 = yes).

service_freshness_check_interval.description: How often (in seconds) Nagios will check the 'freshness' of service check results.

check_host_freshness.description: Whether Nagios will periodically check the 'freshness' of host results (0 = no, 1 = yes).

host_freshness_check_interval.description: How often (in seconds) Nagios will check the 'freshness' of host check results.

additional_freshness_latency.description: The number of seconds that Nagios will add to any host and service freshness thresholds.

enable_flap_detection.description: Whether Nagios will try to detect hosts and services that are 'flapping' (0 = no, 1 = yes).

low_service_flap_threshold.description: The low threshold for service flap detection.

high_service_flap_threshold.description: The high threshold for service flap detection.

low_host_flap_threshold.description: The low threshold for host flap detection.

high_host_flap_threshold.description: The high threshold for host flap detection.

date_format.description: How short dates are displayed (us, euro, iso8601, strict-iso8601).

p1_file.description: The location of the p1.pl perl script.

enable_embedded_perl.description: Whether the embedded Perl interpreter will be enabled during runtime (0 = no, 1 = yes).

use_embedded_perl_implicitly.description: Whether Nagios will process Perl plugins and scripts with the embedded Perl interpreter implicitly (0 = no, 1 = yes).

illegal_object_name_chars.description: Illegal characters that cannot be used in host names, service descriptions, or names of other object types.

illegal_macro_output_chars.description: Illegal characters that are stripped from macros before being used in notifications, event handlers, etc.

use_regexp_matching.description: Whether regular expression matching takes place in the object config files (0 = no, 1 = yes).

use_true_regexp_matching.description: Whether 'true' regular expression matching takes place in the object config files (0 = no, 1 = yes).

admin_email.description: The email address of a global administrator.

admin_pager.description: The pager address of a global administrator.

daemon_dumps_core.description: Whether Nagios is allowed to create a core dump when it runs as a daemon (0 = no, 1 = yes).

use_large_installation_tweaks.description: Whether Nagios will take some shortcuts to save on memory and CPU usage in large installations (0 = no, 1 = yes).

enable_environment_macros.description: Whether Nagios will make all standard macros available as environment variables (0 = no, 1 = yes).

debug_level.description: How much debugging information will be written to the debug file.

debug_verbosity.description: How verbose the debug log output will be (0 = brief, 1 = more detailed, 2 = very detailed).

debug_file.description: Where Nagios should write debugging information.

max_debug_file_size.description: The maximum size (in bytes) of the debug file.
